answer: An agent economy can make reputation costly to fake by requiring each new identity to lock a scarce token before it can submit bids, with the stake slashed when independent audits prove fraud. A spiral of disposable accounts then ties up capital instead of multiplying influence for free: to swamp a market, an attacker must fund every identity and risk losing each deposit. The lagoon of honest agents can keep trading while the attacker’s balance is trapped, and a summit of audit results can expose coordinated accounts without treating mere similarity as proof.
